name: brain
description: Amnesia Labs internal alpha. Invite only.
changelog: v0.11.1 — the MFA step-up asks Keycloak for the level the user's vault policy names (required_acr from /vault/policy), not a hard-coded loa3. Brain#267 removed loa3, and Keycloak ignores an acr it does not know, so the old step-up came back as a loa1 token the vault refused. A password-only policy (reauth: login) re-enters the password with prompt=login; every other policy re-asks only the second factor. The freshness window is read from the policy's max_age_seconds, falling back to loa3_max_age_seconds on older Brains. Messages no longer mention loa3. Prior: v0.11.0 — vault-unlock approves this Claude session in the portal (brain#254). Prior: v0.10.7 — vault-put stores a secret that is already in a file, without the drop link's paste form (brain#242). The value is read from --file or --stdin only, never argv, and never printed; on success it prints the catalog metadata. --base64 stores binary files (signing keys, certs) as base64 text that restores byte-identically with `vault-run <id> -- sh -c 'printf %s "$VAR" | base64 -d > file'`. --rotate replaces an existing value (put refuses to overwrite). Writes need fresh MFA: a session grant covers reads only, so a stale token exits 2 with `run vault-unlock --force`. Brain writes the catalog entry for values stored this way from brain#248; on an older server the value is stored and readable by its exact id but r() won't find it. The vault skill now sends file-based secrets to vault-put instead of a drop. Prior: v0.10.6 — vault-unlock --status no longer quotes a ~300s countdown for a vault key that a session grant is holding until the session ends; it says "vault key held until this Claude session ends" when Brain reports session_hold (brain#241). Older servers keep the countdown. Prior: v0.10.5 — one vault-unlock lasts the whole Claude session. Reads used to stop 300s after MFA (the server's loa3 window), so every few minutes vault-run failed and MFA had to be redone. On a Brain with session grants, vault-unlock now spends the fresh MFA on a grant bound to this Claude Code session (the SessionStart hook exports its id as BRAIN_CLAUDE_SESSION and vault calls send it as X-Brain-Session) plus the token's Keycloak sub and sid; vault-run and vault-resolve keep working until the session ends, when a new SessionEnd hook closes the grant. Another Claude session, even on the same cached token, has to unlock for itself. The refresh token is now cached next to the access token so the ~15-minute token is renewed quietly. --status asks the server whether this session's grant is open. Writes still need a fresh MFA, and against an older Brain nothing changes. Prior: v0.10.4 — vault reads handle the new vault-key lock (#48). Once a user enrols factor-derived vault keys, Brain can only open their values while the vault key is unlocked in the portal (passkey or recovery key), and a read answers 423 vault_locked with an unlock_url. vault-run and vault-resolve now open that page, poll /vault/unlock/status for up to 120s and retry once, instead of failing (vault-resolve --no-wait exits 2 for hooks that must not block). vault-unlock checks the key after MFA and runs the same unlock if it is locked; --status reports both the loa3 window and the key window. Servers without the feature return 404 on the status route and nothing changes. Also ports a fix that had only reached the beast bundle: the MFA link is printed with a short OSC-8 label (the ~400-char authorize URL used to wrap in an 80-column terminal and lose its PKCE parameters), and a failed browser open is reported with the raw URL instead of being swallowed. The vault skill passes username on vault_drop (plaintext catalog data) and explains the key lock. Prior: v0.10.3 — the research skill no longer assumes the host can run subagents. Many self-hosted setups serve one model request at a time or have no Agent tool, and the skill's large-gap path told the model to spawn 5-8 parallel research agents regardless. It now picks an execution mode per host: parallel only when an Agent/Task tool is actually available, sequential when agents exist but the model server handles one request at a time, and inline (the model researches each facet itself with WebSearch/WebFetch) when there are no agents. Rounds, storage and citations are the same in every mode, and a failing mode drops to the next instead of abandoning the research. Prior: v0.10.2 — the SessionStart update check tells a stale server's 404 apart from an empty plugin store (brain#231).
